evidence: Objective 1 (identify properties of cube and cuboid) is fully addressed with faces, edges and vertices listed for both shapes.

Objective 2 (identify properties of pyramids and cones) is fully addressed with a table covering triangular, square, pentagonal and rectangular based pyramids plus a worked hexagonal example, and a cone description.
The teacher's own evaluation questions (vertices of cuboid, edges of cube, tetrahedron vertices, hexagonal pyramid) are all directly answerable from the pack content.
objective_curriculum_alignment.rationale: Both lesson objectives are covered completely and at the depth the teacher intended. All five evaluation questions are addressed within the pack, confirming strong curriculum alignment.

evidence: The pack follows the same two-part sequence as the lesson: cube/cuboid first, then pyramids and cones.
The pack introduces face, edge and vertex terminology explicitly, matching the board-notes approach the teacher used.

The pack goes somewhat beyond the lesson's depth by providing a worked example for a hexagonal based pyramid and introducing a general pattern formula — the lesson plan does not indicate this was taught.
taught_lesson_alignment.rationale: The pack mirrors the lesson's order and emphasis well and reflects a note-taking, board-work style lesson. The additional worked example and pattern discussion are modest extensions that do not distort the lesson but do go slightly beyond what was planned.

evidence: All counts in the table (triangular: 4F/6E/4V; square: 5F/8E/5V; pentagonal: 6F/10E/6V; rectangular: 5F/8E/5V) are mathematically correct.
Cone properties (2 faces, 1 edge, 1 vertex) are correctly stated and explained.
The worked hexagonal pyramid example (7 faces, 12 edges, 7 vertices) is correct and the reasoning given is sound.
scope_conceptual_correctness.rationale: No mathematical or conceptual errors were found anywhere in the pack. The scope stays within JSS1 solid geometry, and the one extension (hexagonal pyramid pattern) is correctly handled.

evidence: Key vocabulary (face, edge, vertex) is defined in plain language before use, making the text accessible to JSS1 learners working alone.
Figure descriptions are embedded in the text so students know exactly what to look at, and the summary table lets students compare shapes at a glance.
The 'Check your work' section provides model answers with brief explanations, enabling independent self-assessment at home.
clarity_usefulness.rationale: The pack is well-structured for unsupported home use: concepts are built gradually, practice questions mirror the teacher's evaluation tasks, and worked answers with reasoning allow students to diagnose their own mistakes.
